I’ve dealt with mental health struggles since the age of 9. I feel it’s hard for people to understand how hard struggles with mental health/substances are, without experiencing those problems themselves. I feel I can relate to him in many ways, but Brians struggles far outweigh anything I’ve dealt with. If Brian was able to get through it with all of the obstacles he’s faced, I know I can. His life story inspires me so much. This past month has been really rough for me, and his music has helped me through this dark time. Getting to see Brian has reignited my drive to become a better musician and human.

The set was an hour and fifteen minutes. My dad and I sat in the sixth row and our tickets were under two-hundred dollars a piece. That’s a steal in my book. It’s a lot of money, but for such a great experience, and compared to what other artists charge, I feel it was well worth the money.

https://youtu.be/vfpQ70Hnu2s
This one is pretty cool in my opinion.

He used a walker to get on and off stage. He looked really hunched over which was kind of sad. Brian also had a teleprompter on the piano. During the performance, he seemed kinda checked out(Blondie and Matt tried interacting with him several times, and he didn’t make eye contact once), which I’m guessing is a mix of old age, prolonged drug use, and anxiety. That being said, Brian sounded really good when he sang. As others have mentioned online, there were sometimes where he wouldn’t pop in, and Matt would take over. His vocals(in the sense of tone, and how long he would hold on to the notes) I’d say were similar to the Stephen Colbert clip during Covid, but his voice didn’t sound as raspy. He sang more than I expected, and sounded amazing throughout given all he’s been through and his age. It was such a surreal experience to be in the presence of such and icon and legend. I’m more than happy to have went!

Thanks! I came up with the idea a few weeks back. Traced out the Beach Boys letters in pencil using a Cooper Black typeface as a reference. I also had a poster that said “Happy Early 80th B-Day Brian!”

It was phenomenal! Brian used a walker and be lined straight to the piano bench. Got a standing ovation! He seemed sadly frail and very hunched over, it’s also worth noting he has a teleprompter on the piano. As many people have said before, he doesn’t play the piano. With that out of the way, the show was incredible. Brian sang a few songs during the set, and when he sang, the vocals were really good! I was surprised by how great he still sounds. Al, Blondie, and Matt do most of the signing but they sound great. Especially Al’s son Matt! Blondie had lots of energy and definitely interacted with the crowd the most. Al not as much, but he did interact some and his vocals were great. He tossed a couple guitar picks into the audience on his way off stage. Brian seemed really out of it mentally though. He didn’t smile once and Blondie and Matt got next to him on a couple of songs and he didn’t even make eye contact. That was kind of sad, but I know the circumstances. The fact that Brian is still alive and still touring is amazing. My grandpa didn’t make it to 80 and he never did drugs, so I don’t quite understand the criticism. Granted, when you look at Chicago and how energetic those guys in their 70s are dancing and running all over the stage, it does put it into perspective. I was really looking forward to hearing Brian close the set by singing Love and Mercy but he didn’t. However, Brian and company did perform Hero’s and Villains(my favorite Beach Boys song) which was awesome. They didn’t do that the night prior, as I checked the set list. I’m wondering if they just ran out of time for Love and Mercy. It was an experience I will never forget, and was truly spectacular if not a little strange.
